surface: .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml (generalize to .plate autonomy.risk_tolerance + low/medium/high tiers + risk:* label enforcement + legacy AUTONOMOUS_MODE compat only when no explicit autonomy section), src/plate_core/autonomy.py + cli.py + plate_config.py (defaults to off when no autonomy section; fix config_report calls, risk rank default, --run/--sleep arg, budget types), .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml risk label + explicit .plate override logic, docs/research + design notes, .agentic/releases fragment (this file)
summary: Generalizes auto-merge + babysit to consult .plate risk_tolerance (Epic #470 / #476). Auto-merge now prefers .plate autonomy section (absent or no autonomy key = fall to legacy marker only, tol low for compat; explicit rt !=off enables graduated tiers; explicit disabled/off in .plate disables without legacy fallback). Enforces PR risk:* labels strictly (exactly one, never critical, rank <= tol; unknown rank to 0). Core fixes for engine (no default enable, fail-closed unknown risk, budget usd as str, local config_report) + cli (require --run explicitly for non-loop, add --sleep-seconds). Addresses multiple review comments on this PR. Template/bootstrap marker removal + full AGENTS.md autonomous prose + full test coverage + procedures are follow-ups per migration_guidance.
migration_impact: Downstream PLATE repositories control autonomy declaratively via the 'autonomy' object in .plate (risk_tolerance: 'off' to fully disable, 'low'/'medium'/'high' for graduated autonomous operation). This is now the core default philosophy (autonomous unless 'off'). The legacy .github/AUTONOMOUS_MODE marker file is sunset: add the .plate section to enable/configure (health and config surfaces will provide migration guidance for repos that still have the marker file). New .agentic/procedures/ directory and built-in procedures are opt-in via the schedules. Template/bootstrap updates remove the marker file from new scaffolds and seed .plate examples. Agents should route autonomous/long-running work through the new plate_autonomy_* surfaces and respect budget/risk signals in .plate.
agent_notes: Autonomy is the default PLATE philosophy and is controlled exclusively via .plate (the autonomy section with risk_tolerance). When present and risk_tolerance != 'off', the plate persona and orchestrator loops should call plate_autonomy_status and plate_what_next first. Use AutonomyEngine (via MCP plate_autonomy_run_cycle or gh plate autonomy run --loop) for continuous operation. Before any heavy step, the governor must be consulted. The legacy .github/AUTONOMOUS_MODE file is ignored for new behavior (migration guidance surfaces it). All engine activity produces PLATE-AUTONOMY-CYCLE or PLATE-PROCEDURE-RUN markers + usage blocks. Procedures run only if their declared risk_level <= configured tolerance. Quiet-operations rules are mandatory for any --loop or scheduled execution. Critical-risk, AGENTS.md/SPEC/credential changes, and need:human-review items are never auto-executed. Agents must not create or rely on the old marker file.
migration_guidance: Add (or ensure) the 'autonomy' section to .plate with desired risk_tolerance ('medium' is a good balanced default for most teams; 'off' fully disables autonomous features). See docs/design/autonomous-plate-engine.md for schema, risk matrix, and examples.
Commit the updated .plate. (Optional but recommended) seed or create .agentic/procedures/ for any recurring work you want the engine to drive.

For repos that previously relied on .github/AUTONOMOUS_MODE: this file is now legacy. The engine and health surfaces will detect it and emit migration guidance. Once .plate autonomy is configured, you may safely delete the marker file (it will be removed from future template payloads and is no longer the source of truth).
Update any custom host scheduler /loop, babysit, or CI invocations to prefer plate_autonomy_status for observability and to respect the risk_tolerance / budget from .plate.
Review and set token_budget values appropriate to your usage and billing; start conservative (the governor defaults to throttle/pause rather than overspend).
In a follow-up PR for this Epic, remove any remaining references to the marker file from AGENTS.md, workflows, features detection, template inventory, and tests.
